newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: $100,000 REWARD FOR ARRESTS OF EXTORTIONISTS
A reward of 100,000 dollars is being offered for information leading to the arrest of the Arnotts biscuits extortionists.
Fifty-thousand dollars is being put up for the reward by both the New South Wales and Queensland Governments.
The New South Wales Cabinet has just approved the reward, and Queensland is expected to announce the same shortly.
New South Wales Police Minister Paul Whelan wouldn't comment on whether there's been any breakthroughs in the extortion investigation.
He says now that the govenments have supported the police in offering the reward, it's now up to them to continue with the investigation.
DICK SMITH WANTS TO TAKE OVER CASA
Entrepreneur and aviator, Dick Smith, says he wants to take over the Civil Aviation Safety Authority, saying the current Board lacks vision and resists change.
A former head of the Civil Aviation Authority, Mr Smith says he can make a difference in the organisation, which he says is acting on rules and regulations from the 1950s.
But he says he'd probably upset a lot of people in the process.
Mr Smith says he understands the Federal Transport Minister John Sharp's wanting to put people on the board who'll act in the public interest.
He says he hasn't been offered a job on the Authority, but has disussed the matter in the past with Mr Sharp.
NSW DISASTER RELIEF FOR NORTH-WEST FLOODS
In north-western New South Wales, the flooded Narrabri Shire will receive funding from the Natural Disasters Relief Program to assist in the rebuilding of washed out roads and amenities.
Damage to roads in the region has been tentatively put at one and a half million dollars...but many are yet to be assessed.
A sea of floodwater is starting to recede in the Wee Waa area, and there's hope road links to the town may re-opened tomorrow.
The main body of floodwater is now moving further down the Namoi Valley into the Bugilbone area.
EXTRADITION HEARING IN SOUTH AFRICA FOR ALLEGED PAEDOPHILE
New South Wales police go to court in South Africa today in a bid to extradite alleged paedophile Phillip Bell.
Lawyers for Mr Bell say they'll contest more than 50 of the charges facing their client.
Police have 215 outstanding warrants for Mr Bell who was arrested last month in the South African beachside town of Jeffreys Bay.

His lawyers contend that under South African law, Mr Bell can't extradited on more than one charge arising from a single event and as such, multiple charges arising from individual incidents should be rejected by the court.
LIFELINE APPEALS FOR FUNDS
Lifeline has launched a fundraising appeal for the first time in the national telephone counselling service's 30-year history.
Chairman, Clyde Dominish, says Lifeline urgently needs funds to expand services, as the organisation has people working in almost every Australian centre.
Today, Hazel Hawke launched a campaign in which thousands of people around the country will be encouraged to hold candlelit dinners on the 8th of March.
Dinner guests will make a donation to Lifeline.
NEW WHOOPING COUGH VACCINE
A new whooping cough vaccine has been released in Australia which results in fewer side effects than the current treatment.
The current triple antigen vaccine for babies called, DTPw, protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and whooping cough.

Professor Clem Boughton from Sydney's Prince of Wales Hospital says unnecessary chemicals in DTPw can now be eliminated to produce a vaccine which is just as effective, but has a lower incidence of side affects.
Last year there were 4-thousand reported cases of whooping cough in Australia.
ANSETT WINS AUSTRALIA-JAPAN RIGHTS
Ansett says newly approved daily services between Australia and Japan will increase flexibility for Japanese to have packaged holidays in this country.
The International Air Services Commission has approved the daily flights by Ansett, and the first will start in April.
Ansett general manager international, Craig Wallace, says daily services will improve flexibility for influencial Japanese tour wholesalers who package and market holidays to Australia.
Ansett has long-argued for daily flights, having operated five services a week on a Sydney-Osaka-Brisbane-Sydney schedule since 1994.
The airline is now trying to increase it's Hong Kong service to daily flights.
OZ URGES KIWIS TO SPEND MORE ON DEFENCE
The Australian Government is urging New Zealand to lift its Defence budget, saying it's current level of 1.1 per cent GDP is unsustainable.
Federal Defence minister, Ian McLachlan, says while New Zealanders don't support high levels of defence spending, it would be in the nation's best interest.
Australia's also been trying to convince New Zealand to buy an extra two ANZAC frigates from Australia.
Prime Minister John Howard announced Australia's defence budget would be quarantined from cuts during his weekend visit across the Tasman.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
